section_outline.heading_intent: Plan your Portugal Wedding, Step by Step
must_answer: Tabs in the DOM (not loaded on click), in this order: When to go; Getting there; Entry rules by passport; Marrying legally by passport; Costs; Planning timeline; Your weekend.
Freshness line near the tabs: 'Legal and cost details checked October 2026, with sources named in each tab.'

WHEN TO GO: 3-row table (Spring, Summer, Autumn) attributed to The Knot (F061); official weather risks: wildfire risk June to September, heat waves July and August, heavy rain October to February (F068); Sintra mists (F062). No September harvest line (F065). Answers PAA 'When can you get married in Portugal?'.
GETTING THERE: Lisbon (LIS), Porto (OPO), Faro (FAO), Madeira (FNC). No flight times (none sourced). US direct routes only after F063 is verified for 2027.

ENTRY RULES BY PASSPORT: AU 90 days in any 180 visa-free, EES fingerprints and photo, ETIAS no confirmed start (F048); US no visa for 90 days or less, 3 months passport validity beyond departure, 2 blank pages (F049); UK 90 in 180, passport issued under 10 years before arrival and valid 3 months after leaving, EES (F050).

MARRYING LEGALLY, all couples: process started online or at any Registo Civil at least one month before the date (F021); valid only once registered (F022); up to six months to marry after the registrar authorises it (F023, IRN, per D1; never the Embassy's three months); documents: ID, birth certificate, certificate of capacity issued within six months or a statement that their country does not issue one (F025); documents in English, French or Spanish need no translation (F026, C03); an interpreter is appointed if needed (F027); witnesses may take part but are not mandatory (F028, C06); both partners must be 18 or over (F030, C07; age line optional); civil, Catholic or civil marriage in religious form (F029); date, time and place agreed with the registrar, out-of-hours and away-from-registry ceremonies agreed in advance (F034).

MARRYING LEGALLY, Australian passport (D3, hedge): Portugal may ask you to prove you are free to marry; the usual documents are a Certificate of No Impediment (CNI) or registry certificates (F035). The Australian Embassy in Lisbon can issue a CNI (F038); DFAT also issues CNIs in Australia (F036, F037). Confirm with the Registo Civil or the Embassy of Portugal in Canberra which document you need and where it must be issued (F041 unconfirmed). Never say an Australian-issued CNI is accepted. Recognition: an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia but in most cases is recognised (F040). Do NOT repeat the Embassy's three-month window or translation rule (F039 conflict).

MARRYING LEGALLY, US passport: the US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a CNI (F042); you sign a statement of eligibility to marry before a consular officer (F043). The USD 50 notarial fee is 'Apply only after sign-off' (Nic, D2); fallback 'a consular notarial fee applies'. At least four weeks processing (F044, re-verify). Never apply US lines to AU or UK couples.

MARRYING LEGALLY, UK passport: if you live in Portugal or another country outside the UK, you do not need a CNI; if the registrar asks for one, show the British Embassy notice (F046). If you live in the UK, use the FCDO online service to see which document Portugal asks for (F045); gov.uk does not say which (F047, hedge).

MARRYING LEGALLY format: numbered 4 steps (contact the Registo Civil; gather documents for your passport; submit at least one month ahead; hold the ceremony and receive the registered certificate). Name the Registo Civil and the CNI in full on first mention. Link 'See the full rules by passport' to /destinations/legal-requirements/portugal only once live (planned_links_when_live).
Registry fee EUR 120 at the registry, EUR 200 outside it or out of hours (F024): 'Apply only after sign-off' (Nic, D2, D4); fallback 'the civil registry charges a fee'.
Same-sex marriage (F031) and the Anglican church line (F032) are left off the hub (T20 page owns them).
COSTS: see add-cost-bands. Plus the venue charges box if not placed in s4.
PLANNING TIMELINE: official minimum is one month (F021). Any longer lead time ('book your venue 9 to 12 months ahead', '3 to 6 months') is labelled as advice, never as a rule (C01).
YOUR WEEKEND: welcome dinner, wedding day, Sunday brunch; what to wear (doc s7 'in the page, not the FAQ'). Related search '3 day wedding packages Portugal'.

questions_to_answer: What are the requirements for getting married in Portugal? (Start the civil process online or at any Registo Civil at least one month before the date (F021); it is valid once registered (F022); up to six months to marry after approval (F023, D1); documents by F025 and F026; then link to the passport rules.)

Can Australian, US or UK citizens marry legally in Portugal? (Rewritten. Yes. AU: the Australian Embassy in Lisbon can issue a CNI; confirm with the Registo Civil or the Embassy of Portugal in Canberra which document you need (F035, F038, F041, D3). US: the US Embassy does not issue a CNI; you sign a statement of eligibility before a consular officer (F042, F043; fee only after sign-off). UK: no CNI if you live outside the UK (F046); UK residents use the FCDO service to check (F045, F047).)

Is a Catholic or symbolic ceremony legal in Portugal? (Rewritten. Catholic: yes, legally recognised (F029). Other faiths: a civil marriage in religious form through a church or religious community established in Portugal (F029). Symbolic: not a legal marriage on its own; many couples marry legally at home first.)

How much is an average wedding in Portugal? (About 100 guests EUR 25,000 to 70,000, named source and date (F069), only after Nic sign-off and doc q6 approval; fallback explains cost drivers with no figure.)

Is a wedding in Portugal cheaper than at home? (No sourced home-market comparison exists: answer without comparisons (F015), give the named Portugal range once signed off, and offer a Wedded Advisor estimate in AUD, USD or GBP. See open question on swapping this FAQ.)
Where is the best place to get married in Portugal? (The 5 regions: Lisbon, Sintra and Cascais; the Algarve; Porto and the Douro Valley; Comporta and the Alentejo; Madeira.)

What are some good wedding venues in the Algarve, Portugal? (Settings, not a venue directory: clifftop, beach with a council or port authority permit (F056), resort, quinta; Albufeira City Council ceremony space (F033); link 'See Algarve weddings' when the child page is live.)

Can you have a beach wedding in Portugal? (Rewritten. Yes, with a permit: the local municipality licenses events on designated bathing beaches, and the Captain of the Port elsewhere on the coast (F056). Not 'extra permits', not 'maritime police'.)
Can your guests stay at the venue? (Many quintas have rooms; exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms and a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee (F059, hedged).)

Can you get married in a Sintra palace? (Yes, through Parques de Sintra at Monserrate, Pena, Queluz, the National Palace of Sintra or the Portuguese School of Equestrian Art (F051); Queluz and the National Palace of Sintra can be withdrawn for state events (F052); nothing fixed to the heritage (F053); Monserrate roof works to Q1 2027 (F054).)
